items.title: Pleb Economist #15: Aleatoric vs. Epistemic Uncertainty
items.text:
This is a post I'd been thinking of making for a while.  It doesn't have a huge amount of practical application, but it does raise some interesting philosophical questions, and could affect how we think/talk about security in Bitcoin.

***

# Aleatoric vs Epistemic Uncertainty

![](https://m.stacker.news/164619)
*Pick a card, any card*

Statisticians / mathematicians / philosophers / scientists have two ways of talking about uncertainty: *aleatoric* uncertainty and *epistemic* uncertainty.

**Epistemic** uncertainty refers to uncertainty due to lack of knowledge. Consider a deck of cards. Which card is on top?  There's a single truthful answer, but we're uncertain what the answer is because we lack knowledge.

**Aleatoric** uncertainty refers to irreducible randomness in a process. If I shuffle the deck of cards and then reveal the top card, what card will I reveal?  There isn't a single answer.  The answer depends on a random process.  The uncertainty arises from the irreducible randomness of the shuffle, not from a lack of knowledge.

The distinction matters for modeling, and thus comes up in economics, finance, physics, and any field in which uncertainty factors into decision making. If uncertainty is epistemic, then perhaps our models can do better by collecting more data. But if uncertainty is aleatoric, then our models can only improve by modeling the randomization process better, not necessarily by gathering more information.

***

# Does Aleatoric Uncertainty Exist?

The trouble with aleatoric uncertainty is that a lot of what we call aleatoric uncertainty might actually be epistemic---we just need to know the information that collapses the uncertainty.

For example, the card shuffling process is perfectly predictable if we knew the initial configuration of the deck, and if we knew the precise movements of the shuffler's hands.

That which we called aleatoric---the card shuffling process---becomes epistemic, and the uncertainty isn't based on an inherently random process, but based on our lack of knowledge regarding the initial conditions of the deck and about the steps used in the shuffle.

***

# The Copenhagen Interpretation vs. Pilot Wave Theory

![](https://m.stacker.news/164622)
*John Bell, who proved that the universe isn't locally real*

So does aleatoric uncertainty exist?  Is there anything at all that's inherently random, where uncertainty isn't simply driven by hidden information?

According to the Copenhagen interpretation of quantum mechanics, the answer is yes. The Copenhagen school says that a particle doesn't have a definite position until you measure it; rather, the particle exists as a probability distribution that only resolves when you measure it, which means the resulting outcome is inherently random.

But the Copenhagen interpretation isn't the only possible interpretation of quantum mechanics. There are others, including ones which collapse the quantum equations from aleatoric to epistemic uncertainty. One such example is "Pilot Wave Theory", championed by Louis de Broglie, David Bohm, and John Bell, which posits that particles have *definite* positions, but that a global "pilot wave" guides their movements in such a way that it results in all the same predictions of standard quantum mechanics. In this theory, if both the pilot wavefunction and the initial conditions of particles are known, then their positions can be perfectly predicted. In this interpretation, there is no aleatoric uncertainty, only epistemic.

So, does aleatoric uncertainty actually exist?  The answer is, it depends what you mean.  If you mean whether the physical laws are inherently random or deterministic, the answer is that we don't actually know. Quantum mechanics is often described as inherently random, but there are fully deterministic models that result in the same predictions, in which the uncertainty is really driven by hidden variables.

But if you mean whether there are processes that in every day life we can treat as good as fully random, the answer is most certainly yes.

***

# In relation to Bitcoin

![](https://m.stacker.news/164623)
*ColdCard and the dangers of low entropy*

Ok, @SimpleStacker, this is interesting, but what does it have to do with me?

Well, aleatoric vs. epistemic uncertainty has applications as it relates to private key generation and security.  When it comes to key generation, everyone always emphasizes that you need a source of high entropy, like a bunch of dice rolls.  Another way of saying that is to say you need a source of high *aleatoric uncertainty*.

But what people often miss is the role of *epistemic uncertainty*.  ColdCard users inadvertently generated seeds with low aleatoric uncertainty, but they weren't hacked for years because no one knew this fact, and thus no one thought to sweep their funds.  They were protected for a time by epistemic uncertainty.

Similarly, I could think of a special sentence that's meaningful to me, but not meaningful to other people, and use a special algorithm to convert it to a number and use the result as my private key. Anyone who knows my special sentence and my special algorithm can derive my private key. There is no aleatoric uncertainty, but because no one knows my special sentence or my special algorithm, my private key can't be guessed.  I am protected by epistemic uncertainty.

The downside of relying on epistemic uncertainty is that it's hard to measure. Which means it's hard to know when you have enough of it.  With random dice rolls, we know exactly how hard it is to guess the resulting number.  But with a sentence that no one knows, or an algorithm that no one knows, it's hard to say how easy or hard it would be for someone else to stumble across the same key. Thus, it's not recommended to rely solely on epistemic uncertainty to protect your keys.

But it's useful to think of epistemic uncertainty as a way to add to your security.  Even if you generate a key using high aleatoric uncertainty, you can protect yourself further with epistemic uncertainty, like not telling anyone where you stored your seed phrase, using decoy wallets, or even by just not letting anyone know you have bitcoin.

items.title: Should Economists Stay in Their Lane?
items.text:
One of the interesting things about studying economics is how wide its applications are. Once you understand general principles like supply & demand, marginal cost/revenue, opportunity cost, comparative advantage, asymmetric information, and so forth, you can apply it to a wide varieties of subjects.

What this has led to, over time, is the "invasion" of other subjects by economists. A list of examples includes:

1. **Politics and Government**- Public choice theory is the study of how incentives affect the behavior of politicians, voters, and government employees. It's produced such foundational concepts as rent-seeking behavior, concentrated benefits & dispersed costs, rational ignorance, bureaucratic incentives, regulatory capture, and the political-business cycle. 

2. **Law and Criminal Justice**- The incentives and tradeoffs inherent to plea bargaining, tort law, and litigation have all been studied extensively through an economic lens. Economist pioneered the concept of optimal deterrence (i.e. how much punishment effectively disincentives a crime, without going too extensive), and written extensively about the negative effects of drug prohibition.

3. **Sports**- Salary caps, the quantifiable effect of home field advantage, etc. all fit right into economics. The best-seller Freakonomics has a chapter about deliberate losses in sumo wrestling (when one party has already qualified for the next round of the tournament, but the other hasn't) that can be proven statistically. 

4. **Healthcare**- Healthcare economics is a massive field, studying issues like moral hazard, adverse selections, and trends such as hospital consolidation. 

5. **Military Strategy and War**- Military conflict is tightly intertwined with game theory. The bargaining theory of war, credible commitment, and other ideas can explain a nation's decision whether to enter or avoid conflict. 

6. **Marriage, Family and Relationships**- Marriage and dating are, in essence, a market based on partner selection and matching. Household specialization can be seen as simple division of labor, and the choice to have children often depends on the opportunity cost of lost wages. Economists will even look at how changes in household income or laws affect divorce rates, or how data from dating apps demonstrate revealed preferences. 

The list goes on and on: religion, sociology, biology, technology all have an economics angle. This has produced something of a superiority complex amongst economists. A [2005 survey of economics graduate students](https://pubs.aeaweb.org/doi/pdfplus/10.1257/jep.29.1.89) found 77% believe that economics is the most scientific of the social sciences. This can be because the mathematical models and empirical techniques used in economics generates more precise predictions than the tools used in political science, sociology and elsewhere, and is capable of distinguishing causal effects from mere correlation. Moreover, incentives are the root of human behavior and many of our actions can be explained by how they personally affect us. 

However, this expansion of economics into other fields, sometimes termed "Economics Imperialism," has produced a backlash. Critics state that economists oversimplify human behavior, ignore research and scholarship elsewhere, and are trying to establish economics as the dominant social science. Sociologists claim "human beings are not merely utility maximizing individuals," and that treating them as purely independent decision-makers responding to incentives is misguided. For example, marriage isn't just a matching market with individuals looking to maximize utility; there's religious norms, romantic preferences, and family obligations to consider. Likewise, political scientists will say that politics is more than rational self-interest, and healthcare experts argue patients are not just units in a cost-benefit calculation. In response to the criticism, some economists claim that other academics are threatened by economics purely out of selfish protectionism and hostility to novel theories that challenge their field's internal dogma. 

So, the question I ask of you is: should economists stay in their lane?

items.title: Austin trip day three: Robotaxi day. Coffee, tacos, and haircuts paid in sats.
items.text:
Hey stackers,

Writing from the hotel after another action packed day here in Austin. I haven’t played poker yet today so here is a Hand breakdown of one I played around midnight last night after making my day two post.

https://stacker.news/items/1603804/r/SatAttack?commentId=1604264

Woke up rather late again but I was fine with that today as I didn’t really have any set plans. Other than exploring and slanging sats I had one goal for today—ride a Robotaxi! They have their own  app which I had installed yesterday and got my account all set up and quickly ordered my ride. You get two choices. A two seater that doesn’t have a steering wheel and has a ton of leg room or a four seater that does have a steering wheel and less leg room (but still plenty). The two seater is always slightly more expensive but I wanted to try that first so that’s what I ordered. It only took five minutes for it to show up to my hotel.

![](https://m.stacker.news/163752)

![](https://m.stacker.news/163753)

Pretty slick looking I thought. But the most impressive part about it by far is the way it drives. It was very cool and I really enjoyed cruising around in this thing. Gave a lot of time to contemplate how this might shape and evolve the future of cities. And I’m torn honestly. On one hand roads and parking take up so much city space and resources to accommodate the car and proliferates infrastructure that makes owning a car mandatory. I love a city built for the walkers and bikers. On the other hand I can’t see this business model doing anything but expanding rapidly. It just worked so so well. The price was competitive to other ride share options, the product worked incredibly, and being alone in there without social friction was really refreshing. It  was really enjoyable to look around the city while some…thing else drove me to my destination.

Which was another Medici Roasters! I needed to start my day with another red eye. As we (the car and I) got closer to our destination I was more and more pleased with my decision to not drive myself. I didn’t know when I  booked but this coffee shop is located directly across the street from University of Texas, Austin. It’s on Guadalupe St. right in in the middle of a big college town. Tons of traffic, people, and shops. No parking. Perfect job for Robotaxi.

This Medici is HUGE. Much much bigger than the previous one and it’s full of students on lap tops and reading books and such. At the counter I ordered my red eye and again I didn’t need to bother asking if I could pay in bitcoin. They had the square terminal with the toggle option. They also had a sign that said “pay with bitcoin” so that’s great. I contemplated asking the cashier lady about people paying with bitcoin but it was so busy and bustling I didn’t want to waste her time. So I silently paid with Phoenix and shortly after walked upstairs with my coffee.

![](https://m.stacker.news/163754)

![](https://m.stacker.news/163755)

I chilled and read and sipped my coffee before heading out on foot to cruise the city I was dropped off in. I didn’t really have an agenda. Quickly though I ended up in a second hand store called 2nd street. They had some nice looking clothes in there and I still needed a dressy undershirt for  a wedding tomorrow. No bitcoin accepted sign there unfortunately but I got a nice shirt for $9.

![](https://m.stacker.news/163756)

Onward into the college town. Nearly every person and building has some Texas Longhorn attire on it. There were frat and sorority houses, all sorts of food and clothing shops, and orange bull heads every where I looked.
Everyone seemed to be anticipating a game between Texas and Mississippi state. I probably should have taken a picture but one fraternity house had a huge sign in the front of it with a football player urinating on what I assume was the Mississippi state mascot. “Go Long Horns. Piss on miss” it said. I walked where ever my mind decided was the direction to go for about an hour before deciding it was time to eat. There was an overwhelming amount of options but one taco stand caught my eye. Closed unfortunately. But that at least set my mind on what I wanted.

So I cruised around sure I would happen upon another source of tacos and lo and behold, I was gifted a spot. It’s called Don Vegas tacos. Tucked away with some other food trucks and brick and mortar food places with benches and ample seating. I notice they have a square terminal and start to get hopeful… could it be?

I took the opportunity to practice my Spanish and ordered five street tacos and a jamaica agua fresca. When she rung me up sure enough the toggle to Bitcoin option was available!! “Yo pago con bitcoin!” I said. Which is a bit broken, but she understood. And she was excited! No one had ever done it before she said. I didn’t talk about bitcoin too much but just explained how some square terminals allow it and some don’t. Another successful lightning transaction, I knew, would make my tacos taste much better. They didn’t need the help though… they were soooo good. Con tortillas hechas a mano  they were so fresh and warm and perfect. I got carne asada. They came with limes and fried onions and cheese and avocado and cilantro. Heavenly. Mi jamaica complimented them very well too. This was a great experience because I was just looking for tacos, not a place to spend bitcoin. But I found both out in the wild.

![](https://m.stacker.news/163760)

![](https://m.stacker.news/163761)

![](https://m.stacker.news/163762)

![](https://m.stacker.news/163763)

I forgot to mention. Earlier in my Robotaxi the screen kept giving me recommendations on different commands to give or ask Grok. “Make the car feel like a sling morning in Kyoto” “what would happen if the moon disappeared” but I decided on my own prompt. “Hey Grok,” “can you give me places where I can spend bitcoin for a haircut?” And it gave me several. It said it referenced bitcoincities.org which I had never heard of. Seems to be some similar  project to BTCmap. Grok gave me three options:

Royalties Barber

Geiser barber

South Austin barber

After finishing mis tacos y jamaica I started to go down the list with phone calls to ask if they do in-fact  accept bitcoin. First call Royalty’s didn’t pick up at all. So I called Geiser. Someone quickly answered and I said I’ve got kind of a weird question… will you accept bitcoin there? “Oh sure I accept bitcoin…” a bit hesitantly. He said it had been a while and only one other person (a repeat customer) had done it. I asked if he used square and he said yes. “That should take care of us” I assured. It was 1 pm and we settled on an appointment time of 330 PM.

So I had a couple hours to kill and decided to go do something I’ve wanted to do since my walk with @Scoresby on day one: rent a paddle board and cruise the river! So I booked my second Robotaxi. I chose the cheaper four door option this time. Again the car was quick to show up and I had another pleasant and impressive drive to my destination. Lady bird lake rentals.

![](https://m.stacker.news/163764)

This little box didn’t accept bitcoin or cash so I had to use a credit card but they quickly had me on my way to the dock on the river. I had to hike a tiny bit but it was pretty out so all good. I’ll let these pictures describe the experience:

![](https://m.stacker.news/163765)

![](https://m.stacker.news/163766)

![](https://m.stacker.news/163767)

![](https://m.stacker.news/163768)

![](https://m.stacker.news/163769)

That bridge is the same bridge @Scoresby showed me that first day where all the bats live. I used it as my turn around point and could hear those bats again. I dropped off my paddle board at about 240 and ordered my third Robotaxi of the day for destination haircut.

![](https://m.stacker.news/163770)

Geiser Barbering was on this quiet street in a cute little commercial building that look to once be a house. Very pleasant experience here. Nick is a master barber and beardsman. He has one single high quality barbers chair and I ordered a straight razor clean shave and a basic haircut in preparation for the wedding tomorrow. We talked a lot the whole time. He was interested in my traveling and poker playing. He has a life long friend who is a full-time poker pro so we related on that topic a lot. Earlier I had seen a “get Elon’s dirty money out of Austin!!” Sign plastered multiple times on the side of a building and was curious what his opinion of the Robotaxi was. He had only done it once as a joy ride with his wife but was equally as impressed as I was.

We talked about bitcoin in Austin and his experience with it. He said he loves accepting bitcoin because it’s free to do so and that he knows a lot of self-identified bitcoiners but none of them like to spend it. He said mainly it’s because they’re afraid of tax obligations. I told him all my favorite parts about bitcoin and I was glad he was willing to accept. He was glad I was willing to pay. He would be using square to auto invert to USD however. We talked a lot about Bitcoin and merchants and what may or may not happened in the future. He said he’d  love it if more people started to spend so that “us merchants” can start to learn and use it more too. He was a cool chatty guy and very willing to have a nice conversation about it.

The straight razor shave was great. He had me all lathered and lotioned and hot toweled and he apparently doesn’t use an alcohol based after shave. It’s for the birds he said. Instead he uses an antiseptic chalk base after shave that feels and works better to seal everything up. I agreed, it was comforting. All spick and span it was time to settle. He uses square on his phone and pretty quickly used it to present a lightning invoice which I paid with no issues. I tipped in cash, saving some sats.

He had mentioned that he some times goes to Medici and I thought it would be cool to ask if I could tip him further with bitcoin and try to get him to spend it on a coffee but I didn’t follow through. The service was a bit pricey already and I was scared to recommend some wallet that I wasn’t familiar with that would be easy for him to use.

I ordered my fourth and final Robotaxi of the day that would conclude today’s adventure and bring me back to my hotel. The ride was a projected traffic-filled thirty minutes but I didn’t mind at all because I knew I would just be chillin and gazing out the window. “RelaxiTaxi!” (IYKYK)

![](https://m.stacker.news/163773)

Instead of window gazing though I asked Grok to pull up my favorite chess grandmaster Eric Hanson. His videos relax me and his chess is wonderful to watch. I’ve been a big fan of the Chessbrahs for many years.

Another great action packed day here in Austin and I’ll be heading out for a few hours of poker very soon.

If you missed day one and two you can check them out here.

Day one: https://stacker.news/items/1602995

Day two: https://stacker.news/items/1603699

Thanks for reading and following along!

items.title: I finally visited Pubkey in Washington DC
items.text:
![](https://m.stacker.news/162019)

I am attending a reunion of sorts of some old friends in DC.  I had some free time yesterday, so I finally got the opportunity to visit the Washington Pubkey.

I have posted a few times about the NYC version. I have a great time whenever I go:

https://stacker.news/items/219987/r/siggy47

https://stacker.news/items/230440/r/siggy47

https://stacker.news/items/1283387/r/siggy47

The Washington DC version of Pubkey is located on 7th Street in the [Penn Quarter](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Penn_Quarter) neighborhood of the city. It's not far from Ford's Theater and the J Edgar Hoover FBI building.  Capital One Arena, where the Washington Capitals play, is down the block. It is an upscale, touristy location.

Pubkey DC opened in January, 2026, according to the website, but I thought it had been around longer.  Yesterday the Washington Capitals had an early game, so there were plenty of fans in jerseys milling about. When I walked in I immediately noticed how different this place was from the New York version. It's huge, around 12,000 square feet, with two bars, a stage, and big screens everywhere showing sporting events. There was a good crowd, which looked to be a mix of tourists, locals, and hockey fans. I can't be certain, but I'm pretty sure I was the only person in the place interested in bitcoin.

This is not an in your face bitcoin space. I had just had a long car and was hungry. I decided to sit at the bar and have some lunch after exploring a bit.

At first I didn't notice much bitcoin stuff, but it is all strategically placed to fit in unobtrusively. I liked the low key design. It could be any sports /tourist spot in any city.

There were a few stickers in the men's room:

![](https://m.stacker.news/162028)

![](https://m.stacker.news/162029)

I then noticed a large wall display with some actively mining bitaxes:

![](https://m.stacker.news/162030)

And this small, but intriguing stack of bitcoin and bitcoin adjacent books below a "Free Samourai" sign:

![](https://m.stacker.news/162032)

I sat at the bar and saw this cool display:

![](https://m.stacker.news/162033)

Occasionally the ticker had a news flash scrolling across the screen.

When ordering my lunch I let the bartender know that I planned to pay in bitcoin. I was told that if I did, I would receive a 21% discount, which is impressive. I asked about the payment setup, and was a little disappointed that they just use square. I tried to.engage my server in a little bitcoin banter, but it was obvious he had no deep interest. I dont want to sound negative. All of the workers were friendly and competent. The menu was similar to the NYC Pubkey. I had a Caesar wrap, which was very good.  I must say paying with the square app was quick and easy. You select the tip amount before the invoice is generated, which is nice. I have experienced a few awkward moments trying to tip at the NYC Pubkey. You never can be sure if the server would prefer sats or dollars. This way they probably get a choice.

That being said, paying with square is still disappointing.

On the way out I found this board near the front bar:

![](https://m.stacker.news/162036)

I guess this proves there are some bitcoiners patronizing the place.

I didn't get to experience an event, but there is plenty of room for bitcoin gatherings. NYC Pubkey always feels a little cramped. I know Thomas Massie will be holding a discussion soon. I hope I get some time on my next trip to catch a presentation.

items.title: Bitcoin Activism (Not a Social Movement)
items.text: **TL;DR:** Here it is! My latest post on Bitcoin. I had this thought long ago, about four years ago, that Bitcoin could be a social movement. I mean, I studied social psychology so I saw some recurrent themes. Well, after four years, I now wrote it and added a lot to the list. Bitcoin is not a movement per se, but small micro-mobilisations that happen here and there, that just happen to use Bitcoin. People come from veeeery different backgrounds, so there are a lot of different actors and agendas at play. The post is long and your attention is short, and you’re most likely not that interested in Bitcoin. Alas, AI is more interesting (ps. me too!). Well, check the photos at least, and skim here and there. I don’t think *anyone* has *ever* written about this topic yet, so it is o r i g i n a l writing! :D

items.title: Trunk or Treat 2026 - This post has free free ecash.
items.text:
# 2024 - snickerbar.me

For Halloween of 2024, I had been experimenting with ecash and was having a blast with stacker.news. I decided to pass out ecash tokens to the parents of trick or treaters to encourage bitcoin adoption in our neighborhood. I forked cashu.me and engaged in some coding that was way over my head and mostly a learning experience for me. The results varied from "eh" to "aight" and fun was had by all. I chronicled that spooky season in [a post exposing my coding ineptitude](https://stacker.news/items/717596), [making a spooky crossword puzzle for stackers](https://stacker.news/items/723313), [iterating](https://stacker.news/items/729712), [mashing up Janet Yellen and Metallica to @DarthCoin's delight](https://stacker.news/items/748546), and ultimately [passing out small amount of sats while playing music by David Lynch on a DX-7](https://stacker.news/items/748618).

![](https://m.stacker.news/56707)

![](https://m.stacker.news/60570)

It was a fun time.

# 2025 - They don't celebrate Halloween in Mossel Bay

South African townships have witches. I never met one, but I heard quite a bit about them, and sadly, it was mostly from scared children. I've been told that the witches are responsible for gangs, substance abuse, and general violence in the townships. What was very sad to me was the amount of talismans I saw children wearing to "protect" themselves from witches. There is a very real bondage there, and as I was in Mossel Bay for Halloween 2025, we kept it low key and at home.

My wife and I personally do believe that there is a supernatural realm, but are thoroughly convinced that talismans, incantations, and other charms do nothing to protect people from evil. So, at home, we kept our American traditions, which are solely for fun and pretend. We made costumes out of paper. The kids did trick or treat to the rooms my wife and I separated to in the two bedroom apartment. We used what was available to make little jack 'o lanterns.

![](https://m.stacker.news/163859)

And in doing so, almost burnt the place down.

![](https://m.stacker.news/163860)

If you're wondering, no, I do not recommend at this point that you fill a gem squash with kerosene soaked fire starters.

We finished the night with some kid-friendly spooky stories. Alas, last Halloween featured no caramel apples, no hayrides, no corn mazes, and worst of all, NO ECASH!

# 2026 - Making up for lost time

The mills of God have done their dance, and now I can...VIBE CODE! What that translates to is a whole new level of usability of this free ecash for my neighbors. Here is [https://snickerbar-me.vercel.app/](https://snickerbar-me.vercel.app/) for 2026. 

Tonight is Trunk or Treat, and boy-howdy, do I have a treat in my trunk.

![](https://m.stacker.news/163863)

![](https://m.stacker.news/163874)

![](https://m.stacker.news/163864)

Now when someone scans a card with their phone camera, they get a temporary wallet right out of the gate with the sats already in it. There is no app or sign-up. Then, with one tap, they can move the sats to a wallet they own (Coinos, Strike, Wallet of Satoshi, Cash App, anything with a Lightning address).

![](https://m.stacker.news/163867)

![](https://m.stacker.news/163868)

# Do it yourself!

So obviously, tonight will be a fun test, but I'm also using this on beggar's night, and you can too! In fact, I've also improved the UI from the issuer's side. You can watch the tokens get claimed in real time:

![](https://m.stacker.news/163869) <sub>As promised in the title, here's your free ecash. First come, first serve.</sub>

I also made, "porch mode" so you can keep a screen up for people to scan one at a time with a little visual hooray with each claim.

![](https://m.stacker.news/163870)

Also, now you can make much bigger cashu tokens in which the QR is actually scannable. I'm thinking of making a few of them humongous so a few people can go buy a shake at Steak 'n Shake.

To get started, fund a wallet and hit \*\*send\*\*. Then follow the steps to making your tokens! Let me know how it goes!

Happy Halloween!

items.title: Freshman Dem Members & Supporters Are Quickly Finding Out The Hill Is Different
items.text:
Earlier today, a colleague brought to my attention that people are rapidly finding out that The Hill does not operate in what I would call a normal way, and that being in the Majority is flat-out hard. Freshman Members arrived in DC over the weekend (and are actually staying at a hotel that is by my apartment.... security is insane) for the 120th Congress Freshman Orientation held in the Capitol.

With the Freshman Members making their first trek to DC since the election is has brought with it a ton of individuals wanting to make a statement. There have been a few rallies and protests in the district that backed this up but yesterday was the first time I saw/an alert was sent out to avoid an area because of these groups. 

Ironically, these people had no idea where they should be because it was aimed at the Expected to Be Speaker Jefferies; however, they had it in a Senate Building. The goal of the groups that were there was to get the Future Speaker to prioritize what they wanted. One group was for reproductive rights, another was for the environment, and I want to say there was a third, but I can't remember what their priority was. Now, these were clearly Democratic supporters; however, the Capitol Police soon had to start arresting them... because they started to fight each other over who was correct in what should be the priority..... I kid you not.... Grown adults who support the same person.... fighting each other because they want their thing to be the priority.... all while they are on the completely wrong side of Congress.... Just incredible. 

Thinking back, that should have probably been a sign to me of the things that were to come. Yesterday was also the first day I saw on TV various Senators, in particular, speaking out against Sen. Chuck Schumer becoming the Senate Leader. Which absolutely blows my mind. If you factor in the two outstanding races flipping Dem, you end up with a 9-seat flip. This would be the largest flip since President Eisenhower was in office in 1958. It would be the largest since the U.S. was 50 states. 


The idea to then take the person who was in charge of Senate Dems and, in a lot of ways, punish him by not giving him the promotion that comes with leading your party to victory would frankly be insane. For better or worse, Schumer has been Leader of the Senate when he had to deal with Trump being the President, and to put someone else in that role frankly seems like a backhanded move. During a time when the elections resulted not only in a party flip but also in many who won in Republican areas being much more middle-of-the-road, installing a leftist favorite in Van Hollen doesn't exactly make the most sense. Likely future Speaker Jeffries is facing the exact same issue when he was able to reverse Republican/Trump 2024 inroads with various groups and make the Democratic Party have a much larger tent. 

Nowhere is the absolute meltdown of the far left and leftists more evident than on the Instagram account "Dear_White_Staffers." This account is well known on The Hill by both sides due to the far-left propaganda they post. Over the last few years, since I have followed them, they have really ended up losing the plot on a lot of things, and when the American people would vote, and it turns out things like open borders were not popular, the account would kinda melt down. Now the same thing is happening once again because Democratic Leader Jeffries sent out an email reminding the freshmen that the funding that he and his leadership team have done got them into office, and it was under his leadership that, frankly, the Party was able to accomplish such a landslide just a week and a half ago. 

Apparently, these Freshmen and their supporters thought that they could take the money, networks, endorsements, etc. that Leader Jefferies gave them and not pay the piper. While it does seem that most of the Freshman House Members understand this, their supporters are losing their collective minds. 

Across both the House and the Senate, particularly in the Democratic Party due to their party rules, traditions, etc., seniority is a huge, huge thing. To be honest, it makes sense as well. I mean, it is often the case that new members do not have the connections or understanding of why some things are the way that they are, and the catastrophic issue that would occur is that various laws and statutes would suddenly and dramatically change. So many of the people on both sides miss this critical issue, and when they run into it rather than tell anyone why they changed, they just pivot or blame the system. The system can be changed; it just isn't a quick fix, and Members on both sides and in both chambers want quick and easy wins. 

There is a post on Dear_White_Staffers that is from someone named _meganthuy that highlights how narrow-minded these leftists are. In her post, she came out bashing the Moderates of her party (those that you know represent the red states and red areas that Democrats won it) because those individuals, multi-term winners and freshmen included, do not want the party to go overboard and immediately make moves to abolish ICE, cut all funding to Israel, outright ban frontier AI and data centers, etc. She said that these issues are the reason that the moderates won, ignoring the clear data that showed that, frankly, prices are too damn high and Republicans have failed to lower them plus got them into another war. 

This 20-something thinks that you can enact far-left legislation while failing to do the math, just like Republicans did with the SAVE Act. If you can deal with fragmenting your party in the House, you still need 60 Senate seats, and frankly, Dems don't have it. That's before we even get to the whole the President is Donald Trump issue, who has said he has no issue vetoing things. 

This girl further goes on to say that there were a lot of people who reluctantly voted Democratic and that they did so only to stop the war, but immediately follows it up with these much further-left ideas, like abolishing ICE instead of reforming it. Throughout the video, she highlights how they won because of XYZ but then follows it up by ignoring those things and focusing on things that do not address XYZ that got those Democratic Members elected. 

I thought with a margin of victory as large as the House and Senate were that the internal division issues that both leaders would face would fall by the wayside, but apparently... that's not the case. As a result, I see two possible outcomes, and that is either common sense wins out, and the far left goals will be reigned in or the far left is going to blow their legs off by nuking the best-suited person to deal with the wide array of groups representing the party and nuking the idea of passing anything for the next two years. Whoever is the leader of the House and Senate is going to have to be people who want to get a deal done, plain and simple. Trump is known as someone who loves a deal, and if you remove the dealmakers and place combative people who clearly are not going to cut a deal, like these outspoken internet people and people currently on The Hill, your end result is going to be two wasted years, with the Republican Party able to identify and leverage unpopular issues against Dems two years from now.

items.title: Austin trip day one: Bitcoin all around
items.text:
Evening stackers,

I write from my hotel having just checked in and showered after a very long productive day.

I landed in Austin at 1045 AM and I had rented a Turo. It took me a frustratingly long time to find the damn thing but once I was was in the right garage (blue  not red) I found it pretty quickly. Then I went to my hotel, a grungy little thing 15 min south of round rock, only to be told I couldn’t check in for another 1.5 hours. I was looking forward to a shower and a nap before heading out to meet @Scoresby at PlebLab. No matter, the poker room The Lodge Poker Club was only a 13 min drive away. I could kill some time there no problem.

![](https://m.stacker.news/163462)

![](https://m.stacker.news/163463)

![](https://m.stacker.news/163464)

The place was really nice inside with plenty of tables and friendly staff. After getting my players account all set up  I waited for 20 min or so to get seated at a 1/2 500 max no limit Texas Holdem game.

The game was good and the players were friendly. I posted a breakdown of my favorite hand in the saloon here:

https://stacker.news/items/1602411/r/SatAttack?commentId=1602968

They had a table of treats for sale perhaps made staff member and I am sucker for both pastries and supporting small business so—win win. I got the pumpkin spice cake with cream cheese frosting (delicious). Here it is:

![](https://m.stacker.news/163465)

I only played for 1.5 hours and instead of going to the hotel to check in I headed straight to town to meet with @scoresby and @k00b which I was a bit nervous about. I’m not a very social person. But I was doubly excited to not only meet some real life bitcoiners, but fellow stackers! The pm stackers who created and build this place no less ! So off I went, nerves be damned. 

I found PlebLab easy enough. It’s a cool small space with ultimate hacker vibes. Scoresby and Koob came to say hey right away and were very cool and friendly. Koob wasn’t wearing any shoes, which is apparently normal for him, and as a fellow barefoot person, I give triple salute. Shoes suck. I’ve been a barefoot person my whole life and I too am barefoot at work every day. Kudos to Koob. He gave me some cool SN stickers and a cooler SN hat and pretty quickly Scoresby and I embarked on a city walk. I wish I would have thanked Koob for his founding and effort for curating this Bitcoin internet social for all of us but sadly I forgot.

It was very very cool talking to scoresby, what a guy. We had a lot of bitcoin related things to talk about which is so (pardon my French) fucking refreshing man. This is rare for me. Maybe for you too, dear reader. To be able to talk to a bitcoiner about bitcoin is so much fun. We can jump to this conclusion or that realization because we understand exactly where we are coming from in certain outlooks, opinions, knowledge, and world views. Scoresby is the man. He took me all around and showed me where there has been some awesome sounding Bitcoin events in the past. He showed me where the unchained head quarters is. He took me to Waller beach where walked along the Colorado River for a good ways. He showed me a bridge where apparently millions of bats live and come out at night in huge swarms. We could hear them chittering away. We saw a turtle. We saw a woman chatting on the phone in the grass with a HODL shirt on. Cool to see out in the wild, we both agreed.

He was quite curious about my poker playing and if someone is asking my about poker I have a hard time noticing anything else. So my recollection of surrounding details on the trail is a bit shoddy. I can rant and rant on that topic. I had a great time chatting it up and really appreciated his time taking me around. I loved talking and breathing bitcoin like it was a normal part of every day life. I felt submersed in its community just by chatting it up. We talked about the direction he would like SN to go and his efforts to make it happen. We spoke about current security incidents, cold storage options, SN sending wallet option past and present cultural shifts… it was great. Often I feel like I am the only real life bitcoiner out there when I’m surrounded by people who don’t know or don’t care but here in this moment, I felt the opposite. Perhaps it was the combination of being in a new city, talking to a new person, and seeing new things, but it felt like bitcoinization has already happened. It was normalized. We were the normal ones…

After an hour of walking we parted ways and it was time for me to EAT.

@plebpoet had suggested I go to a BBQ place called The Green Mesquite. “The real ones” go there she said. So not wanting to risk being a shoeby, that’s where I went.

![](https://m.stacker.news/163466)

![](https://m.stacker.news/163467)

Now the first thing I deeply appreciated was they had their own parking lot!! If you’ve ever been to Austin you know that parking here may be the only thing comparatively scarce to Bitcoin. The place has a real Texas saloon vibe to it and I thought just maybe this place has been here just as long as Austin. The man at the counter was friendly and had me sit anywhere. There was only one other person there. There were lots of old Texas decorations and Older country and blue grass songs playing which I appreciated. (Don’t like this new stuff in that genre)

I quickly decided that the best route would be a BBQ platter so I could try as many different things as possible. I went with the three meat choice and got smoked brisket, dark meat chicken, and sausage. My sides were green beans and fried okra and I got a shiner bock to wash it down with. Here it is:

![](https://m.stacker.news/163469)

Everything was delicious. I don’t know WHAT is going on with their BBQ sauce, sitting unceremoniously and unlabeled with all the other condiments, but it was amazing. It wasn’t crazy sweet and complimented the chicken and brisket so very well. I didn’t try on the sausage as I didn’t feel the need. It was so juicy and flavorful.

As I’m sitting finishing my beer something really wonderful happened. I saw a man through the window walking up, dirty and skinny and disheveled. He came through the door and I was too far to hear the words exchanged but I’m fairly certain he asked for a meal and said he couldn’t pay for it. Without anger or hesitation the guy working the counter said “I can do a sausage roll” and made him a small meal. The roll, some chips, and a water.

It was really wholesome and I can honestly say I’ve never seen anything like it.

I left shortly after and sat in my car and pulled up BTCmaps to see what sort of trouble I could get myself into. Just 7 min drive away there was a place listed called Local Pastures. Here is their BTCmap and website:

[https://btcmap.org/merchant/node:10791261306](https://btcmap.org/merchant/node:10791261306)

[https://www.localpastures.farm](https://www.localpastures.farm)

![](https://m.stacker.news/163470)

![](https://m.stacker.news/163471)

![](https://m.stacker.news/163472)

![](https://m.stacker.news/163473)

These guys are awesome! It’s a tiny little store the size of a large Kobe’s box and they get local meats, dairy’s, produce, and coffee and sell them here. When I walked in the first thing I noticed was their square terminal. They have the flip version. I poked around for maybe only a minute before asking the man if they accept bitcoin and he said “yep no problem.” Ha! Another victory for the books. Now it’s time to shop. Unfortunately the majority of their stuff required a kitchen to get use out of but the selection was quite nice. I had to settle for snacks. I got a couple of beef sticks and some pecans by two separate local farms.

![](https://m.stacker.news/163474)

When it was time to ring up he remembered I wanted to pay with sats and pretty quickly generated a lightning invoice before flipping it over to me. Easy day. Phoenix wallet again didn’t disappoint in speed and success. I asked him if he had ever heard of BTCmaps and he said no. I let him know that’s how I found this image and gave a brief explanation about what it is. He thought it was pretty cool when I showed him. I also asked if anyone else spends bitcoin there he said maybe once a month. He did say that for some stretch of time in the past there was a guy who would come 1-2 times a week and spend his sats there but he moved away. Perhaps that guy is a stacker. 

We had spoke a bit back at PlebLab about how disappointing BTCmaps can be. It definitely does not paint an accurate picture of where you can find places to spend your hard earned sats. So it felt good to get one first try. Maybe I’m lucky? Maybe I have a knack for finding the spots? Really I just liked that this one had a carrot as their symbol on the map and it was conveniently close by.

All in all, great day. I will now take a quick power nap and head back to the poker room for a couple hours of table time.

Day two post coming tomorrow!

items.title: Austin trip day two: I ask to pay with bitcoin and someone tried to choke me
items.text:
Hey stackers,

Writing from the poker room after a four hour session. Taking a long break before I head back. Here’s my favorite hand from the sesh if you’re interested:

https://stacker.news/items/1603097/r/SatAttack?commentId=1603670

I woke up later than I wanted to knocking on my hotel door. It was 930 and housekeeping wanted to clean my room. I politely declined, got out of bed, brushed my teeth and quickly made my way out. There were things to see and bitcoin to spend. @plebpoet had recommended Caffe Medici as a place you can buy coffee and pastries for sats so that’s where I went first. There’s three locations and with some poking around I found the origional one. It’s in a nice quiet part of town and the ambience from outside looked really cool.

Here’s their BTCmap: [https://btcmap.org/merchant/way:382559089](https://btcmap.org/merchant/way:382559089)

![](https://m.stacker.news/163624)

![](https://m.stacker.news/163625)

I loved these stone chairs and tables. I wish I could have captured them all but some were being used and I didn’t want to take pictures of strangers. Inside was really nice too. Lots of plants and plenty of seating. I head to the counter where I see their square terminal and order a red eye which if you don’t know is an espresso shot with a regular coffee poured over it. It will clear the mind and wake up the bowels. Good for the morning. Right in the middle of asking if she would accept bitcoin she rings me up and answers my question; I see that wonderful toggle in the top left of some square terminals. I toggle to Bitcoin and I’m presented with a lightning address. I pay it with Phoenix no issues.

I asked her how often people pay with bitcoin—not very often, I guessed. She said only some times. She had been working there for four months and I was the third person to pay with sats. Not bad actually, I thought. It’s not like she rings everyone up, so there could have been others.

After a few sips of coffee and a couple pages from the second book of the Outlander series by Diana Gabaldon, I realized I had forgotten to check the parties! Fool boy. I asked where they came from, I don’t remember the name, but they get them from a local bakery here in Austin. I ended up with a blueberry muffin and toggled over to Bitcoin and sent another successful transaction.

![](https://m.stacker.news/163627)

![](https://m.stacker.news/163628)

I had plans to go to jiujitsu at the Austin 10th planet at 11 but waking up late was really deterring me from executing that plan. I really wanted to skip the workout and stay on this couch with my book and coffee. I read and read some more and checked the time. It was 1030. The gym was only 15 min away. There was time to not skip…. Over to my left I notice they have whole beans for sale on the shelf and decide there. I’ll
Buy some beans and stop being lazy. After the third lightning transaction in the last hour she tells me you get a free coffee with a bag of beans purchase….. UuuUgh it really sounded nice to sit and read with my free cup. Instead I take it to go and head to the gym.

![](https://m.stacker.news/163629)

I arrive at the gym 10 minutes before class time. I didnt bring a rash guard so I needed to buy one and told the guy over the counter as much. I asked if I could pay for both with bitcoin and he was a bit hesitant. “I think so” he said. He’s showing me the options for rash guards that are hanging on the racks when I see a box on the floor with some orange and black material inside. The box is labeled “b-coin”

Are these rash guards?! I ask
Oh yeah, they are. You want one of those?
Uuuuh YEAH. He pulls one out and shows it to me and it’s AWESOME. Here it is on me:

![](https://m.stacker.news/163630)

He had to text the owner and inquire about my bitcoin request. She responded pretty quickly and texted him a QR code made by cash app. The ones that you can pay either lightning or on-chain to. I took the opportunity to save some liquidity from my Phoenix channel and paid on-chain with Blue Wallet. I told him he should let her know I made an on-chain payment and that I was confident she’d be ok with that. And that she should receive the payment in about ten minutes. I paid 3sats/vB to ensure that was accurate.

Equipped with my new sweet rash guard it was time to start class. Everyone was very welcoming in introductions and we got to work pretty quickly. We warmed up with some bridges and shrimps and got right into the lesson. Today we were going to work on getting a hip toss from full guard and failing the attempt some attacks you can do instead.

My partner was great, I wish I remembered his name. I’m fairly novice, and he was patient and helped me with some important details on the attacks we were learning. We went over locking the Americana after the failed hip toss, then the guillotine, the triangle, the kimura, and omaplata all stemming from the original hip sweep attempt from full guard. during practice  I took a nasty elbow to the lip that swelled right away and filled my mouth with an iron taste (wear a mouthguard kids). Lesson complete, the next hour was open mat. They started the 5 min repeat clock and let people get sparring rounds in. I did a couple before hit hitting the showers. I’m a bit out of jiujitsu shape haha. Awesome stuff. Awesome class. Thanks coach Curtis!

![](https://m.stacker.news/163631)

On my way out the gym coach Curtis was at the front desk. I had asked him earlier for this group picture and told him I will
Blog about my day today on a forum. “Blog or vlog?” He asked.

Blog.

“People still read?” Haha YES I told him. And I told him where I’d blog as well I told him about stacker news and what it’s like. I told him the idea that because valuable things are used to express like-ness valuable content surfaces to the top. I showed him my stacker news and made a couple zaps. He was really intrigued. “A negligible amount I assume, like a small amount of sats?” Ummmm YES SIR. I was happy to hear him use the word sats. Bitcoin was normal for him, it seemed. He said he will check it out and that seemed like the perfect opportunity to give him one of the SN stickers @k00b gave me yesterday. He loved the sticker and joked about putting it up on the stall door so people were forced to see it. I’m sure he was joking but I really hope that happens. Then he asked me if I was the guy who paid with bitcoin today. I said yes and he goes “ok let me hook you up” (!!!)

He said anyone repping and using bitcoin he wants to help out. Wow… awesome. He starts digging around in the “b-coin” bin looking for a pair of shorts to give me. They didn’t have my size, unfortunately, and so he offered a long sleeve rash guard instead. I had to decline. I have many rash guards back at home and I didn’t want to take one just because it was free. He told me I can come back to the gym for free while I was on my trip… I was so grateful. How cool! He showed me around the gyms grocery store which was actually rather stocked. They had grass fed beef. They order by the cow and sell frozen beef from the gym. They had raw milks and other treats. Loaves of bread. All sorts of locally made goods. He told me the raw milks were made by a lady who loves bitcoin and sometimes they use Bitcoin to transact with her. Hooter Flats was the name of her company. I bought one of the chocolate milks. Perfect post-training snack.

![](https://m.stacker.news/163632)

Workout complete I wanted to head to play some poker but I needed to eat first. I pretty quickly decided to head back to the Green Mestique from yesterday and get the same thing but different meats. I ordered the turkey, chopped beef, and the sausage. I had to get that sausage again. For sides I got potato salad and repeated the green beans as well. When they brought my plate they had given me chicken  instead of the turkey. No matter, I knew it was great. I couldn’t resist putting the BBQ sauce all over the chicken even though it stung like hell the cut on my inner lip. But I worked through the tears and finished strong.

![](https://m.stacker.news/163634)

And that’s day two! I went to the poker room after this and I am just now starting another session. I’ll probably play a couple hours before heading to bed.

If you missed my day one report check it out here: https://stacker.news/items/1602995/r/SatAttack

See you stackers, thanks for reading.

items.title: Plenty of success with square bitcoin payments.
items.text:
Hey guys. Wanted share a nice place on Solomon’s island Maryland called Juice buzz if you’re ever in the area. Here’s their BTCmap: https://btcmap.org/merchant/node:13576086075

I spend bitcoin there often and I am still running into new staff members at the register there. They have the toggle option that makes everything so easy and smooth. I just had a nice interaction and wanted to share.

They make their own great juices so I got one of those and they do smoothies as well. I got a berry blast with creatine. When the lady rung me up she said scan or tap and I responded with the same thing I always do here:

Actually I’m gunna pay with bitcoin, isn’t that cool?

That is cool! She exclaimed, which made me smile.

So she presented the pay page, I toggled to Bitcoin, and having pre-opened my Phoenix wallet I scanned it right away. I like to hold the phone up so they can see me press pay and witness the speed.

She gasped and said Wow that was really fast!

Right?!

Then I like to give a cool spiel that always seems to be accepted well without me feeling or acting like a salesman.

I told her that jack Dorsey is the creator of cash app and also square and he is a nice advocate for bitcoin—new information for her.

I told her what’s cool here is that we are using an inclusive network. Before, in order to interact with a Cash App bar code, I would need cash app. Venmo to Venmo. Cash app to Cash App. Examples of exclusive networks. But what’s cool about Bitcoin is anyone can use it and in many different ways. You can use any one of the hundreds of apps out there like I did or if you have the skill and desire you can build your own and interact in the same way we just did.

She was interested! But she did say skeptically: yeah I’m not really too sure about bitcoin.

I said that’s understandable. It’s weird and intimidating and controversial and there’s lots to learn.

I continued to say one of my favorite things about Bitcoin though is that anyone can use it. Your age, sex, race, religion, location matters not. Bitcoin will work for anyone without permission or ID.

She asked: but do you need cash app to have Bitcoin?

No, Bitcoin is completely separate from everything else I said. And left it at that.

Juice buzz is owned by Dana the owner of the Blue Wind Gormet. I wrote about her and that place twice in the past. Here’s the links:

https://stacker.news/items/1436254/r/SatAttack

https://stacker.news/items/1472530

These places right now are my favorite places to spend sats. As far as I know Dana is still keeping the bitcoin she receives through her square terminals and isn’t converting. I have tried to encourage her to buy honey from [https://sweetsats.io](https://sweetsats.io), a bee farm in Maine, to use in both of her stores so she can have somewhere to spend her sats, but I don’t think it’s happened yet.

items.title: Austin trip day six: lakes, hikes, final bitcoin meal.
items.text:
Hey stackers,

I write from the airport terminal in route to the chilly easy coast. What an incredible trip this has been. I’m normally looking forward to getting back home and returning to the recurrence of every day life. Not this time. I am not ready to leave and I know I’ll be back. Perhaps to live one day.

Yesterday morning I woke up at 3 AM a little hung over from all my wine at III forks and I couldn’t sleep. So I went to play poker. Got there at 4 AM and the crowd was wild. Everyone had been there since the night before and everyone seemed drunk, tired, or both. I played this huge hand and ended up winning a $1400 pot. https://stacker.news/items/1606387/r/SatAttack?commentId=1606424

I played until about 7 AM and headed out for breakfast. I ended up at a really nice diner called Phoebes diner and had a great meal. Forgot take pictures though. They sell slab bacon and serve it in thick deep fried slices. Wonderful. I get back to the hotel and sleep from 830AM to 12PM. @grayruby had recommended I take the 30 minute drive to visit lake Travis. After poking around on my phone for things around there I found a hike and a restaurant I wanted to do.

Here’s the all trail for the hike: [river place nature trail](https://www.alltrails.com/trail/us/texas/river-place-canyon-trail?sh=true)

The hike ended up being a great success. The weather was great and it was just the right amount of challenging to get the heart pumping.

![](https://m.stacker.news/164323)

![](https://m.stacker.news/164324)

I’ll take a little time to plug the Earth Runners here. For all my barefoot maxis out there this is a wonderful footwear for rocky environments where bare feet may have a tough time. I have taken these everywhere in all sorts of terrain. Love them.

![](https://m.stacker.news/164326)

![](https://m.stacker.news/164327)

![](https://m.stacker.news/164328)

![](https://m.stacker.news/164329)

![](https://m.stacker.news/164330)

Awesome hike. I was pleased to find good water flow and was surprised how clear it was! That tree going across the path is called the noggin knocker and there was a sign warning you not to knock your noggin haha.

Finishing my hike I was very ready for food and water and headed out to a restaurant right on Lake Travis called The Oasis. I didn’t really know what I was getting myself into but this place was GRAND. It’s a massive four story restaurant that’s the size of a big hotel. All four stories have a balcony that over looks the lake. There’s awesome art and decorations everywhere.

![](https://m.stacker.news/164331)

![](https://m.stacker.news/164332)

![](https://m.stacker.news/164333)

![](https://m.stacker.news/164334)

![](https://m.stacker.news/164335)

On my way in there was this blue metal UFO thing covered in stickers. I took the opportunity to put one of the stickers @k00b gave me on there. Turned out nice I think.

![](https://m.stacker.news/164336)

![](https://m.stacker.news/164337)

The food was decent. I got the chips and salsa. (Great chips!!) the chicken enchiladas with rice and beans, and a margarita on the rocks. I wasn’t planning on drinking but… the view made me.

![](https://m.stacker.news/164338)

![](https://m.stacker.news/164339)

I got back to my hotel around 6 pm and slept until 830. I had been deliberating between going to play poker one last time or going to find one last place to spend some sats. The issue was they were in opposite directions and I was really torn for a while. With one last check of BTCmaps I found a great solution. A place called Rockin Rolls that wasn’t in the downtown areas! It was close enough to the hotel and poker room to do both. So off I went. Here’s the BTCmap link [https://btcmap.org/merchant/node:13309320506](https://btcmap.org/merchant/node:13309320506)
It’s a small food truck in small gathering of food trucks right off the road. I appreciated the abundance of parking here!

![](https://m.stacker.news/164342)

![](https://m.stacker.news/164343)

These guys are awesome and if you’re a pizza eater in Austin I recommend giving this one a try. They make sourdough pizza rolls and they are very good. I ordered three classics (pepperoni and cheese) and a mini cannoli. Now time to pay. I see they only have the small white square terminal and I won’t be presented with the toggle option so I tell the man I’d like to pay with bitcoin if I can… he isn’t sure and calls the owner over who was thankfully there. He says “I think I set that up …” and we collectively poke around the terminal. Doesn’t take us long to find Bitcoin listed as one of the payment options and I tell them all we have to do is click that and it should generate me a QR code. It did and I made another seemless Phoenix payment. I gave my small spiel about how cool this is and how anyone who knows how can interact with this terminal with a bunch of different options.

The owner, Jake, was impressed and pleased. He was excited to see bitcoin being used and told me I was the first to do it. But on BTCmaps someone had verified the location in November 2025 so I was thinking perhaps not. I showed him BTCmaps and his little page on there and he thought that was very cool too! I told him that I would be blogging about this day and experience on stacker news and gave him the lowdown about what goes on here. “That sounds right my ally” he said. He loves community and according to him he likes crypto. He’s an ethereum guy he says. I told him I don’t know anything about it because I haven’t been able to move past Bitcoin. I was explaining what SN was and he understood immediately. “So instead of a like you just send over a little satoshi?” YEAH! I gave him a SN sticker and told him how to find us and that if he ever had any questions or inquires about using bitcoin in his business or other wise this is the place to come. I told him he would be very welcomed as a business owner accepting sats.

When I got my order I realized I didn’t have a drink. I asked for a bottle of water and had opened my Phoenix wallet to pay but he just said don’t worry about it. Thanks Jake!

I’ll say again, if you like pizza, come try this place. It’s awesome and he was telling me he’s looking to move to another state. Him and his wife love Austin but they’ve been there for 20 years and are ready for change. So time is running out!

![](https://m.stacker.news/164347)

After my pizza rolls it was time for one last poker sesh. I headed back to the lodge card club and played an uneventful 1.5 hours and won $10. I got gas for  the Turo rental, got to my hotel around 1130, and packed up. I had to be up at 530 to head to the airport.

I enjoyed my time in Austin very much and I really enjoyed sharing my experience here on stackers!! I’ve gotten a lot of support and a lot of engagement and that has been sweet. Thanks for reading and thank you to those who gave me awesome suggestions. I tried to do them all.

items.title: [Read-along] The Odyssey, W.H.D. Rouse, Books I - III
items.text:
*Below I am starting the book club, as promised previously. It has probably taken longer than I originally led on. I expect that this can be forgiven. Whether you took up the challenge or not, there may be something for you in the following post. I have made an effort to give some original thoughts, followed by a character list and book summaries. As mentioned before, I am reading a hard copy of the translation of W.H.D. Rouse, but I can also recommend the* [*digitized version of the translation of A.S. Kline.*](https://www.poetryintranslation.com/PITBR/Greek/Odhome.php)

***

# leading themes and ideas

* post-war society leads to excess and decay
* culture, values, family, country -- all need to be defended by their inheritors
* the most commonly held belief is not always the correct one

# Commentary

The first three books show how Telemachos has been living and responding to the apparent death of his father, Odysseus. Unbeknownst to Telemachos, his father is lost at sea, dealing with cyclops, and upsetting Poseidon in the meantime. With the help of other greek heroes (Achilles, Agememnon, Nestor, Menelaus etc.), Odysseus led the Achaeans to victory at the battle of Troy, and since then, things have not been going so well back home. This is the setup for the poem.

This is a story of what happens in the aftermath of war, when a great society produces heroes that defend its culture and norms against outsiders, and how, despite their victory on the battlefield, this same culture must be defended in their absence. This is seen at the outset, when the gods discuss what has become of the house of Atreus, whose son, Agememnon, finds himself the victim of Agisthos. The latter is eventually murdered by Agememnon's own son, Orestes, in an act of revenge for the murder of his father and the destruction of his household. Zeus laments the fact that, although they have brought this terrible fate upon themselves, men continue to hold Zeus to account. Wherever the fault lay, the poem tries to reckon with the phenomenon where society grows weak in the absence of the warriors who will defend their culture.

As the drama of the poem ensues, it is revealed how political infighting led the Achaeans to split up after Troy, leaving Agememnon and Odysseus away from their homeland. In the latter's absence, his wife Penelope and his son Telemachos have been left to defend what is left of his household. Suitors consume Odysseus' wealth, as they loiter, courting Penelope.

**So far, I have taken the following from the poem, summarized in a few sentences:**

* A great culture, such as the Greeks had, will produce great warriors, in whose absence its greatness will quickly fall to shambles.
* There will always be those willing to feast on the spoils bought by the sweat and blood of another person's brow
* Even when an entire population believe one thing, it may not be true. Truth is not easily discerned, but found out through persistence, struggle and adventure.

So, to you, reader of Epic poetry, I ask the question:

* Where do you see yourself on this cycle (i.e. good times --> weak men --> bad times --> strong men?)
* Is there an analogue in modern culture to the suitors feasting on Odysseus' wealth?

***

# Reading notes:

key characters

* Odysseys: a great warrior from Ithica. Never returned from the battle of Troy, in which he earned his stripes as a hero.
* Telemachos: the son of Odysseus.
* Penelope: the wife of Odysseus. Awaiting Odysseus' return.
* Suitors: men gathered in Ithica, enjoyers of Odysseus' house and belongings, as they vie for Penelope's hand in marriage.
* Zeus: Father of the gods. Feels let down by mortal men because of what happened in the aftermath of the battle of Troy concerning Agememnon.
* Aigisthos: killed Agememnon and married his wife. Is then killed by the latter's son, Orestes.
* Agememnon: in the aftermath of the battle of Troy, did not wish to sail home, for fear of displeasing Athena. He splits from Diomedes and Nestor, and stays in Troy
* Athena: Zeus' daughter. Favors Odysseus, intervenes for him so as not to see his house come into ruin
* Poseidon: god of the seas
* Mentes/Mentor: Athena in the form of a man, advises Telemachos in Ithica and in Pylos.
* Aigyptios: Wise councilman, blesses Telemachos
* Nestor: son of Neleus, king of Pylos.

# Book Summaries:

## Book I

> These men amuse themselves with music and song, freely, since they consume another’s wealth without repayment, one whose white bones are tumbling in the waves, or rotting in the rain on some far shore
> \--Mentes.

Zeus and Athena meet on Olympus. Lament Agememnon's murder and betrayal by Aigisthos. Athena descends from Olympus to intervene into the affairs of Telemachos, to keep him from a similar fate. His father, Odysseus, suffers the ire of Poseidon, who keeps him from returning home against the will of the other gods. Suitors, who think Odysseus is dead, harass Penelope and Telemachos, and take advantage of the latter's good manners. No one really knows whether Odysseus has died. Telemachos answers Mentes that he does not stop the suitors from courting his mother for the dread of not knowing what has come of his father. Before transforming into a bird to depart, Athena rouses Telemachos to gather the lords together and order them to stop, and moreover, that he should go out in search of his father.

## Book II

> ‘My lords, my Suitors, though Odysseus is dead and you are eager for me to marry, have patience till I complete this work, I do not want it wasted, this shroud for noble Laertes, ready for when pitiless death’s cruel end overtakes him: since I fear some Achaean woman of this land would blame me, if he who won great wealth lay there without a shroud.’
> \--Penelope

Telemachos assembles the lords of Ithica and makes his case, demanding that and end be put to the suitors' behavior. Antinous rebukes him, saying that Penelope has tricked them for the past three years, by saying she would choose a husband when the finishes weaving the shroud of Odysseus' father, Laertes, which she would work on during the day only to unravel the work she had completed under the darkness of night. Zeus sends an omen portending the destruction of the suitors. Athena again urges Telemachos to go in search of his father, provisions a ship and a crew for him, and even afflicts the suitors in Telemachos' home with drowsiness. Telemachos sets sail for Pylos in search of news of his father.

## Book III

Telemachos arrives at Pylos, where the people all pay sacrifice to the gods. Telemachos and Mentor make an offering to Poseidon, in Nestor's name. Telemachos appeals to Nestor, who also fought at Troy, to give news of what happened to Odysseus. He reports that the latter was caught in the middle of a feud between Menelaus, who wished to depart after the battle of Troy, and Agememnon, who feared the angering the gods, and wished to wait. Nestor and Odysseus went with Menelaus, leaving Agememnon behind. In a moment of hesitation, however, Odysseus turned back to join Agememnon. Nestor and Menelaus sail from Troy together and in the meantime, Aigisthos overtakes Agememnon, killing him and taking his wife for marriage. Nestor urges Telemachos to look on the heroism of Orestes, who took revenge against and murdered his father's murderer, Aigisthos. He tells Telemachos he needs to visit Menelaus for news of what came of Odysseus. Nestor offers Telemachos his men and ships, his hospitality, they sacrifice a heifer to Athena, and set off at dawn.

***

items.title: Exact-Channel Circular Rebalancing for Alby Hub
items.text:
Not sure who else might need this, but...

I built Grynvault Rebalance on top of Alby after the swap-backed rebalance option I used to use disappeared since boltz went down. I still had liquidity, but on the wrong sides of my channels—and ordinary routing could not guarantee which local channel sats would leave through or return through.

RC.7 is an experimental Alby Hub v1.24.3 fork for embedded-LDK operators. Choose the exact outgoing and returning channels, find a non-paying local route, review a fresh fingerprint-bound quote and projected balances, then approve one execution. It includes fail-closed migration and recovery hardening from upstream review.

It cannot create liquidity or guarantee a public route: you need one channel with outbound liquidity, another with inbound capacity, and a viable path.

macOS 15.4+ for this RC. PGP-signed manifest; not Apple-notarized; independently maintained; not official Alby.

Source/download: [https://github.com/hudhaifahz/hub/releases/tag/grynvault-rebalance-v0.1.0-rc.7](https://github.com/hudhaifahz/hub/releases/tag/grynvault-rebalance-v0.1.0-rc.7)

items.title: Bitcoin Arena: decentralized game & prediction market platform live on testnet4
items.text:
Hi there,

We built Bitcoin Arena: games and prediction markets on Bitcoin. It is fully decentralized. There is no company running the rounds, no central server and no custodian. Anyone can run a node, and anyone can offer an app. It’s live on testnet4, and we need people outside the team to try both.

There’s no token and nothing to buy. Test sats are free and have no value.

Anyone can run a node

* Install it on Windows, macOS or Linux. A setup window walks you through it.
* Post a bond on Bitcoin and take a seat.
* Host apps, verify rounds and earn a share of the fees.
* No permission needed. Your bond is your ticket in.

Anyone can offer an app

* Write your game and sign it, and any node can host it.
* The nodes replay every round with your rules.
* There’s no approval and no listing fee.
* You earn 2% of every paid round in your app.

How a round stays honest

* A Bitcoin block hash draws the committee of nodes, so nobody picks who decides.
* Stakes lock in a Fedimint federation run by the nodes.
* A result counts only when 5 of 7 nodes confirm the same one, and anyone can object for 10 minutes.

How you can help

* Run a node on testnet4 and tell us where setup was hard.
* Build a small app and tell us what’s missing in the docs.
* Play Tick Tock Next Block, Rock Paper Scissors or the 15-minute Bitcoin Up or Down market and try to break it.

Would you run a node or build an app on this? If not, what’s stopping you? Honest criticism helps us most. Reply here or join us:
